misconception_description: Student believes that in the expression x == a or b, the comparison operator distributes to both operands of the or operator.

  if d1 < d2 or 0 then

metadata.modification_notes: The student added input validation to handle edge cases where the array is empty or has only one element. They wrote `if n == 0 or 1:` believing it means "if n equals 0 or n equals 1", but it actually evaluates as `(n == 0) or 1`, which is always True since 1 is a truthy value. This causes the function to always take the early return path and never execute the main sorting and number-building logic. The student genuinely believes this is the correct way to check if n is either 0 or 1, and thinks their code properly handles these edge cases while allowing other cases to proceed to the main logic.
